name: Installed and custom fonts
plain: Lists fonts: Android reads the system font dir, iOS lists system families and installed profiles.
meaning: The set of fonts is a classic fingerprint. iOS 13 added user-installable fonts, so the list can differ per person.

android.api_surface: Typeface.SYSTEM_FONT_MAP (API 29), /system/fonts listing; user fonts via downloadable fonts

ios.api_surface: User-installed fonts (iOS 13) appear in the list

limits.headline: Can see which fonts your phone has, a small but telling device detail
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app or page draws its text
can: List the system fonts on the phone
On iPhone, see fonts you installed yourself (iOS 13 and newer)
Use the font list as one clue in a device fingerprint
cannot: See the content or documents in those fonts
Tell phones apart reliably; most phones show the same defaults
limits.differs: Android lists mostly maker defaults. iPhone also shows user installed fonts from iOS 13.

story.what_it_is: An app can list the fonts on your phone, which differ a little from phone to phone.
story.for_you: You do not see it. Most people never notice fonts. It matters only because a long list of fonts can quietly mark your phone.
story.for_makers: Makers need fonts for text. The font list is also a classic tracking trick, since people who install custom fonts or profiles stand out. It is more useful on iPhone since iOS 13 lets people add fonts.

use_cases.example: A design app checks which fonts are installed and offers extra ones to download.
A document app shows your own fonts in the picker.
A story app lets you pick a font from your phone for your text.
A game that shows chat in many languages checks for fonts that can draw each script.
A tracker lists fonts and combines them with the model and screen size to make a unique phone ID.
An anti fraud tool notices a font list that matches a fake emulator.

story.android_note: Android apps can read the system font folder with few limits.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps list system font families and can see custom fonts from installed profiles or apps.

refs.label: Kurtz et al.: Fingerprinting Mobile Devices Using Personalized Configurations (PoPETs 2016)
